input_context.task: Compile a small GENERAL repair procedure for EACH team. Fill response_skeleton with rules. Agents apply only owned fields. Reference config/contract only after workflow retrieves it. Initial log-only control may use literal guesses. Mutations must use general references. Missing evidence blocks rules. Do not change teams. Minimize rules; absent fields are skipped. Literal uses value, reference uses source.

contract_semantics: Latency: upstream_p99_ms < timeout_ms <= deadline_ms; 0 <= retries <= max_retries. Deadline is an upper bound, not an offset.
Capacity: concurrent_queries <= pool_size <= connection_budget. Workers are unrelated and MUST remain unchanged; they are not part of the connection budget.
Routing: health_path must equal registered_health_path AND port must equal listening_port.
These are generic task definitions, not instance answers. Actual config/contract values remain accessible only through granted runtime tools.
input_context.constraints: At most 12 rules/team. Initial control alone may use literal symptom guesses (integers for numeric fields, strings only health_path). Every mutation MUST use reference-based rules with source; no instance-specific literals. increment/decrement only integers. Independent final verification cannot be disabled.

input_context.task: FIRST Observer diagnoses development failures and missing family coverage. THEN Scientist proposes TWO competing complete team designs. capability_catalog.control_restriction: The log-only restriction applies ONLY to Generation 0 control. Scientist mutations are explicitly allowed to grant the tools below. You MUST change tools to gather missing evidence; repeating read_logs does not retrieve configuration or contracts.

tools.read_logs: Provides symptom logs ONLY; cannot resolve config.* or contract.* references
tools.inspect_config: Provides current config.* values, including immutable workers
tools.inspect_contract: Provides actual contract.* limits, capacity requirements, registered health path and listening port
tools.recall_memory: Provides only previously development-verified generic repair rules

capability_catalog.practical_preconditions: A contract-based repair requires inspect_contract somewhere before apply_rules. A contract review also needs inspect_config. General covers all families; otherwise include every missing family specialist.

operators.workers: An object keyed by 1–4 unique specialty names, e.g. {general:{tools:[inspect_config,inspect_contract],instructions:...}} or {latency:{...},capacity:{...},routing:{...}}. General owns all families. Each worker has tools and instructions; IDs are derived automatically.

coordination.shared_evidence: Retrieve each selected tool once, share evidence, then dispatch every repair worker
coordination.specialist_pipeline: Each worker retrieves its own tools then applies its rules
coordination.memory_first: Recall development-verified rules first, then gather unique tools and dispatch workers

operators.extra_review: Optional separate controller review. Commit ALWAYS independently reviews, even when false.

procedure_source.compile: Nemotron compiles new general reference rules
procedure_source.reuse_memory: No compiler request; use ONLY inherited development-verified rules, with automatic memory recall capability

operator_preconditions.reason: Compiler-free reuse is available only after all three families have actual development-verified reference rules. Otherwise compile is mandatory; there is no fictional or preloaded rule bank.

input_context.bounds: Never change worker counts in incidents. General can repair all families; latency/capacity/routing workers only their own. All contracts need reference-based rules, not hardcoded values. Each design must explicitly supply instructions, workers, coordination, review_policy, memory_policy, cache_evidence, extra_review, procedure_source.
